title: Complex behavior is rare but present in small Turing machine spaces

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Complex behavior is rare but present in small Turing machine spaces

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Starting from a blank tape, roughly one in 50,000 2-state 4-color Turing machines and one in 200,000 4-state 2-color machines show complex behavior, and 14 essentially equivalent machines among the 2,985,984 with 2 states and 3 colors do so.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Among such 2-state 4-color Turing machines perhaps one in 50,000 shows complex behavior when started from a blank tape.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 11, “The Notion of Computation”; section “Universality in Turing Machines and Other Systems” (from p. 706), p. 709. Scope: 2-state 4-color, 4-state 2-color and 2-state 3-color Turing machines

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch11-29: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: All transition tables can be regenerated exactly, so no external empirical data are missing. Reproduction is straightforward after matching conventions, though the qualitative complexity threshold introduces interpretation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate all machines in the stated finite spaces under the book's numbering and blank-tape convention, run each to a declared horizon, quotient by specified symmetries, and classify complexity with prespecified recurrence and growth metrics.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Complex behavior' is not uniquely defined.

Counts can depend on runtime cutoff and equivalence conventions.

data adequacy: 0.85

analysis feasibility: 0.8

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The 2-state 3-color census is a finite computation that has a definite count once complexity is formalized, and the figure of 14 equivalent machines is a specific target. The two larger rates are explicitly approximate and depend on a sample and a classifier. Reproducing the order of magnitude is feasible; pinning the exact quoted rates is not, because the predicate is not fully formal.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From a blank tape, enumerate the 2,985,984 machines with 2 states and 3 colors and sample the much larger 2-state 4-color and 4-state 2-color spaces. Using a fixed complexity test, estimate the complex fraction and count the equivalence class of complex 2-state 3-color machines. Rates near one in 50,000 and one in 200,000, and a class of 14, support the report; a count of a different order refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Complex behavior is a visual category, so two reasonable classifiers can move the estimated rates.

The one-in-50,000 and one-in-200,000 figures are sampling estimates, and the spaces are too large for a naive full run at long times.
